Psalms 77 · Psalm 77: I Will Remember the Works of the Most High

points: The psalmist cried unto God with his voice and God gave ear. In the day of his trouble he sought the Lord; his sore ran in the night and ceased not, and his soul refused to be comforted. He remembered God and was troubled, and complained that his spirit was overwhelmed.

note.label: Psalm 77: I Will Remember the Works of the Most High

points: God held his eyes waking, and he was so troubled that he could not speak. He considered the days of old, the years of ancient times, called to remembrance his song in the night, communed with his own heart, and his spirit made diligent search.

note.label: Psalm 77: I Will Remember the Works of the Most High

points: He asks whether the Lord will cast off forever and be favorable no more, whether His mercy is clean gone forever, whether His promise fails, whether God has forgotten to be gracious and shut up His tender mercies in anger.

note.label: Psalm 77: I Will Remember the Works of the Most High

points: He calls this his infirmity, then resolves to remember the years of the right hand of the Most High. He will remember the works of the Lord, His wonders of old, and meditate and talk of His doings.

note.label: Psalm 77: I Will Remember the Works of the Most High

points: The Most High's way is in the sanctuary. There is no god so great as our God, who does wonders and has declared His strength among the people, redeeming with His arm the sons of Jacob and Joseph.

note.label: Psalm 77: I Will Remember the Works of the Most High

points: The waters saw the Most High and were afraid, and the depths were troubled. The clouds poured out water, the skies sent out sound, His arrows went abroad, His thunder was in the heaven, and the lightnings lightened the world while the earth trembled and shook.

note.label: Psalm 77: I Will Remember the Works of the Most High

points: His way is in the sea and His path in the great waters, and His footsteps are not known. He led His people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
